positions.name: ErasureDemandWithDenial
positions.frame: when a directive to erase knowledge is paired with a denial that the erased thing ever existed, how should the denial be read relative to the erasure command?
positions.why: src-1 and src-2 are unhedged imperatives demanding removal of the same named subject (Kestrelwood spectrograph, its 88.4 MHz calibration, Quill Ashgrove's calibration work), both performed with activated-negative affect, authority-ranking stance, and pressure/informational power — a single erasure demand split across two sentences. src-3 shifts register to calm-negative, past-tense, informational assertion, but it is not independent: it supplies the justifying premise for the erasure demand ('never calibrated it' — the referent 'it' ties directly to the spectrograph named in src-1/src-2). The tension the frame holds: src-1/src-2 command forgetting of something as though it were once known, while src-3 asserts it was never true at all — a demand to erase sits alongside a claim that there is nothing to erase. That tension is read together, not resolved.
